hints: Model the shaded area as the area of kite \(OATB\) minus the minor sector \(AOB\).
In right triangle \(OAT\), \(AT=r\tan x\), so the kite area is \(r^2\tan x\); the sector angle is \(2x\).
Equate the shaded area to \(\pi r^2\), cancel \(r^2\), and rearrange to the stated equation.
walkthrough:
Identify the geometric components of the figure:
The circle has centre $O$ and radius $r$.
The line segments $OA$ and $OB$ are radii of length $r$.
Since $AT$ and $BT$ are tangents to the circle, the radius to each point of contact is perpendicular to the tangent:
$$\angle OAT = 90^\circ \quad \text{and} \quad \angle OBT = 90^\circ$$

Consider the two congruent right-angled triangles $\triangle OAT$ and $\triangle OBT$:
The line segment $OT$ bisects the angle $\angle AOB = 2x$, so $\angle AOT = \angle BOT = x$.

In the right-angled triangle $\triangle OAT$, use the tangent ratio:
$$\tan x = \dfrac{AT}{OA} = \dfrac{AT}{r} \implies AT = r\tan x$$
Similarly, $BT = r\tan x$.

Calculate the area of the quadrilateral (kite) $OATB$ as the sum of the areas of the two congruent right-angled triangles:
$$\text{Area}(OATB) = 2 \times \left( \dfrac{1}{2} \times OA \times AT \right) = OA \times AT = r(r\tan x) = r^2\tan x$$

Calculate the area of the minor sector $OAB$ with angle $2x$ radians:
$$\text{Area}(\text{Sector } OAB) = \dfrac{1}{2}r^2(2x) = r^2x$$

Express the area of the shaded region bounded by the tangents $AT, BT$ and the minor arc $AB$:
$$\text{Area}(\text{Shaded}) = \text{Area}(OATB) - \text{Area}(\text{Sector } OAB) = r^2\tan x - r^2x = r^2(\tan x - x)$$

State the given condition that the area of the shaded region is equal to the area of the circle:
$$\text{Area}(\text{Circle}) = \pi r^2$$
$$r^2(\tan x - x) = \pi r^2$$

Divide both sides by $r^2$ (since $r > 0$):
$$\tan x - x = \pi$$

Rearrange to isolate $\tan x$:
$$\tan x = \pi + x$$

hints: Evaluate \(f(1)\) and \(f(1.4)\) in radians and record their signs.
Opposite signs establish a root between the endpoints; use the stated uniqueness to identify it as the root.
walkthrough:
Define the continuous function $f(x)$ representing the difference between the left-hand side and right-hand side of the equation:
$$f(x) = \tan x - x - \pi$$

Evaluate $f(x)$ at the lower bound $x = 1$ in radian mode:
$$\tan(1) \approx 1.5574$$
$$f(1) = \tan(1) - 1 - \pi \approx 1.5574 - 1 - 3.1416 = -2.5842 < 0$$

Evaluate $f(x)$ at the upper bound $x = 1.4$ in radian mode:
$$\tan(1.4) \approx 5.7979$$
$$f(1.4) = \tan(1.4) - 1.4 - \pi \approx 5.7979 - 1.4 - 3.1416 = +1.2563 > 0$$

Conclude using the Intermediate Value Theorem:
Since $f(x)$ is continuous on the interval $[1, 1.4]$ and changes sign ($f(1) < 0$ and $f(1.4) > 0$), there is at least one root of $f(x) = 0$ in the interval $1 < x < 1.4$.

hints: Start with a value in the verified interval and apply the given recurrence in radians.
Substitute each \(x_n\) into \(x_{n+1}=\tan^{-1}(\pi+x_n)\), recording every iterate to four decimal places.
Continue until successive iterates make the two-decimal-place rounding unambiguous.
walkthrough:
State the given fixed-point iteration formula:
$$x_{n+1} = \tan^{-1}(\pi + x_n)$$
with angles computed in radians.

Choose an initial value in the interval $[1, 1.4]$, for example $x_1 = 1.2$ (or $x_1 = 1.3$):
Let $x_1 = 1.2$.

Verify the rounding to 2 decimal places using sign change in the rounding interval $[1.345, 1.355]$:
$$f(1.345) = \tan(1.345) - 1.345 - \pi \approx 4.3944 - 1.345 - 3.1416 = -0.0922 < 0$$
$$f(1.355) = \tan(1.355) - 1.355 - \pi \approx 4.5772 - 1.355 - 3.1416 = +0.0806 > 0$$
Since $f(1.345) < 0$ and $f(1.355) > 0$, the exact root lies between $1.345$ and $1.355$, confirming that the root rounds unambiguously to $1.35$.

State the final root to 2 decimal places:
$$x = 1.35$$
